The thesis is a reflective commentary of the creative practice of non-linearly following ginger. It is available in ORE at https://hdl.handle.net/10779/exe.34592232

The interactive film was compiled using Korsakow authoring tool. It can be opened and viewed using the "How to access the Korsakow film" file. It is composed of 100+ audio-visual clips ordered with a randomised logic by the Korsakow's algorithm. The film is a microcosmic function of rhizomatic relativism, offering a window into how a web of relations can non-linearly emerge through the lens of ginger.

description:
This film is the creative output of a practice-based PhD titled "Following: From the ghats to plains - Stories that make ginger".

The project follows ginger to defetishise it by making its more-than-human relations visible. The practice attempts to do so by exploring ginger’s entanglements with the Western Ghats and its ecosystems at risk, a UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site.

The assumed within-South following is decolonised in rhizomatically exploring ginger’s movements, instead of the traditional tracing of the thing’s commodity chain between Global South-North. The practice, therefore, becomes non-linear, decentralised, and non-hierarchical thing following, starting across three different regions around the Western Ghats of Karnataka (India) and moving along paths emerging in situated knowledges across field sites. In the process, the research affords new ways of understanding ginger’s diverse becoming across its value systems.

Examining the ecology of relations that binds ginger with people and the environment they reside in, as a sensory apprentice, I pursue the discourses of multi-sited ethnography, interactive documentary and polyphony to explore my practice as a creative mediation of ginger’s assemblage and the public. I rely on interactive documentary’s non-linear and multi-perspectival affordances to create a montage of juxtaposition of un- and under-represented alongside privileged voices of the assemblage. The resulting audio-visual output takes the shape of a Korsakow film, exploring its offline capacities to convene screenings as alternate spaces of public discourse. The communal screenings with the Korsakow film takes shape of a sympoietic system of sensorial polyphony. Where the becoming-with the Ghats takes place by blending of digital with the visceral, for the multiple voices of the more-than-human participants and the audiences converge and create shared site-specific experiences. The screenings mediated as a dialogic space, brings stakeholders to deliberate over the emergent relationships, and motivates committing to actions that directly or indirectly address the exigencies that become visible.

Although not transpiring as designed, the research nonetheless develops around the adaptive environmental, cultural and political changes needed to address degradation within the region’s critical ecosystems. It contemplates, in conclusion, how rhizomatic and sensory influences of non-linear following and interactive documentary can create a confluence of sense making through affective and cognitive perceptions to influence sustainable change-bearing actions.
